author: Chicago City Wire
title: Chicago Contrarian criticizes Ald. Will Hall over response to Walgreens Chatham closure
text:
Chicago Contrarian said May 5 that Ald. Will Hall failed to denounce crime concerns after Walgreens announced plans to close its Chatham store.
The statement came after Hall held a news conference outside the Walgreens at 8628 S. Cottage Grove Ave., where he called for the company to be charged with “first-degree corporate abandonment.” Chicago Contrarian criticized Hall’s response and said he failed to denounce criminals connected to shoplifting at the store, according to Chicago Contrarian .
Walgreens confirmed that the Chatham location would close because the store had higher levels of theft and violent incidents than its other locations, making it difficult to maintain a safe environment for employees and customers. Residents and officials protested the closure during the rally hosted by Hall, according to the Chicago Sun-Times .
Walgreens has closed or announced closures of multiple locations on Chicago’s South and West sides in recent years, including stores in the Chatham area and nearby communities. Some residents have raised concerns that the closures could limit access to prescriptions and everyday retail needs in affected neighborhoods, according to the Chicago Sun-Times .
The Cook County State’s Attorney’s Office charged 2,585 retail theft cases in 2025, up from 1,073 cases in 2024. The Illinois Organized Retail Crime Association also reported increases in violent retail crime incidents involving weapons threats and injuries, according to CBS News Chicago .
Chicago Contrarian was founded in August 2019 and publishes commentary on urban policy, crime and governance issues affecting Chicago. The outlet says it provides analysis on law and order, politics and local affairs in the city, according to Chicago Contrarian .
